newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Delhaize says in Indonesian venture.
newsitem.headline: Delhaize says in Indonesian venture.

text.p: Belgian retailer Delhaize said on Tuesday it had signed a long term cooperation agreement to develop a large supermarket chain in Indonesia with the Salim Group there.
This second agreement follows an announcement on Monday that Delhaize was to set up a supermarket chain in Thailand with local partners.
Under the Indonesian accord Delhaize would provide technical assistance and allow Salim Group to use Delhaize's Le Lion logo.

Salim Group owns 10 supermarkets, of which seven are in Jakarta, two in Bandung and one in Surabaya. The supermarkets will be renamed "Super Indo" and integrated in a company named P.T. "Lion Super Indo", Delhaize said in a statement.
"It is the intention of Salim Group to further develop its supermarket chain in Indonesia since this country has a substantial and increasing potency," Delhaize added.
It said the Indonesian chain would benefit from Delhaize's expertise.
Salim, with a 1996 turnover of about $15 billion, is the largest privately controlled business group in Indonesia, which also has investments in other countries in the region.
Delhaize, which already has interests in Europe and the United States, said the agreement was in line with its plan to develop a strong presence in Asia.
It reiterated that its strategy was to concentrate on its core business, food retailing, to develop the group through alliances and cooperation with local partners and to favour long term growth.
